So rework depth is computable from an archived bundle, with no new record and no `run/` directory.
**Probed across the archive** (all 63 bundles, 2026-09-04): **58** have a `run-ledger.xml`, **46** hold `attempt` events, **all 46** carry `WriteEvidence`, **39** show rework depth > 0, **392** attempts in total. Only **10 of 63** still have a `run/` directory, so a loose-event reader would see almost nothing — the ledger is the only path that works retroactively. The probe omitted `isProductChurnPath`, so those figures are a **superset** including governance paths; a real report must apply the filter and re-measure.
**What is actually missing.** A **reporting surface**: `C-REWORK-CIRCUIT` emits churn only inside an escalation message (`src/grace-cursor.ts:2716-2721`), per task, at trip time. Nothing reports it per bundle, and nothing reports it across the archive. The size-at-snapshot question F141 left to the maintainer is **still open and now optional** — rework depth answers the ceremony-cost question without it, and F141's own reasoning already argued depth is the truer signal.
**Position 5 of five in the 2026-09-04 order**, re-scoped to the surface, not the record.

Finding.Title: ### F156 — every approved spec's `Constraints` carries an authoring-pass instruction that is false once the spec is frozen. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-04** by parsing all 63 archived `spec.xml` (root `NgraceChangeSpec`, bundle id as its only child element), with whitespace flattened first because the phrases wrap across lines — a line-oriented grep misses `C-EVIDENCE-DISCRIMINATION`'s occurrence entirely.
**24 of 63** archived specs carry authoring-pass text, and **all 24 occurrences sit inside a `<Constraint>`** — none anywhere else in the document. By phrase: `authoring pass` **24**, `until the spec is approved` **13**, `status remains` **12**, `do not author plan.xml` **7**. By root status: **20 `applied`**, **4 `superseded`**. It recurred in **all three** bundles of 2026-09-03.
**Why the position is the defect.** `Constraints` is read as the scope contract — the authority reads it that way when approving, the executor reads it that way when implementing, and a plan is measured against it. A frozen `applied` spec whose Constraint says *"status remains draft; do not author plan.xml until the spec is approved"* states three things that are false of the artifact containing them. The instruction is true only during the authoring pass it names, which is over before the spec is ever read again.
**No ruling put it there.** `grep -n "authoring pass" decisions.md` returned **0 matches** before this entry, so the habit was never recorded, and [F4](#f4) (`decisions.md:175`) mandates two-stage authoring without ever asking for the boundary to be written into the spec. There is nothing to overturn — this is the authority's brief habit reaching an artifact it does not belong in.
**Cost, stated honestly.** **Zero tool findings.** No lint rule, review detector or validator fires on any of the 24, and none can cheaply: detecting it means matching prose, which this house treats as a defect in its own right (`review.regex-over-structure`). The cost is paid in human attention — a ruling paragraph in each of the three plan briefs of 2026-09-03, telling the executor to disregard a Constraint of the spec it was implementing.
**Two remedies, and the first costs nothing.** (a) The authority stops writing temporal instructions into `Constraints` from the next spec brief onward — the boundary belongs in the brief, which is where the executor takes its sequencing from. (b) The durable half is a rule in `skills/ngrace/ngrace-spec/SKILL.md` and its packaged mirror: `Constraints` holds durable scope facts; authoring-pass sequencing is the brief's and the gate's. **Skill text is product**, so (b) is a bundle. Chartered as [`C-CONSTRAINT-DURABILITY`](#named-bundle-registry), **position 2 of five** in the 2026-09-04 order. The 24 archived specs are **not** rewritten: an archived artifact is a dated record.

Finding.Title: ### F158 — the supersede verb's contract, measured, and one non-atomic failure path. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Probed **2026-09-04** on a throwaway project against the real CLI, because [D27](#d27) makes this verb the only route for a defective approved artifact and the authority had never driven it.
| question | measured | |---|---| | replacement state required | **only that its directory exists** (`spec new` is enough) — draft status and absent `plan.xml` are both accepted; the verb does not gate on the replacement's ceremony | | missing replacement | refuses, exit 1: `Replacement C-PROBE-B is missing as a directory under active/ or archive/.` | | abandoned bundle's artifacts | `spec.xml` and `plan.xml` root status → `superseded`, and `<Replacement>ID</Replacement>` injected as the first child of the bundle element | | open epoch | **folded by the verb itself** — loose `run/*.xml` events land in `run-ledger.xml` under `<Epoch-N>`, `run/` is deleted, `run.xml` and `run-ledger.xml` remain. No separate `cursor fold` is needed | | directory | moved `active/` → `archive/` | | `supersedeChainDepth` | incremented on the **replacement** (0 → 1), **not** on the abandoned bundle (stays 0) | | `reRatificationCount` | **untouched on both** — so a re-ratified bundle carries its count into the archive permanently | | source code | **never touched** — `supersedeChangeBundle` (`src/gates/ledger.ts:1383-1481`) writes only the two governance files' status plus the rename, and rolls the bytes back on failure. This substantiates the help text's *"Discards governance, never code"* |
**The defect worth naming.** A supersede that **fails** mid-verb can still leave a side effect: with a cursor allocation too narrow to cover the events being folded, the fold errored (`event 2 outside every allocation … unterminated range`) **after** appending a loose `run/N-T-001-discarded.xml` event. The final rename rolls back cleanly, but the fold-then-write boundary does not, so a failed supersede is not a no-op. Not on the governed path for a properly allocated epoch, and not chartered here; recorded so the next session that sees an orphan `discarded` event knows where it came from.
**One incidental confirmation.** The probe ran the CLI from the working tree, which already carries `C-SCOPE-AUDIT-ATTRIBUTION`'s unshipped production, so its `review --change` of the archived bundle printed `Scope audit: not-run — plan for C-PROBE-A resolved under archive/` — mechanism B working end-to-end on a real bundle before it has shipped. Read as evidence for the mechanism, not as shipped behaviour.

Finding.Title: ### F159 — the criterion that names a forbidden mutation cannot observe it, in the bundle built to close exactly that class. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-05** at `ba10f2b` with the implementation in the working tree, by mutating a full-tree copy under `/tmp` and running `bun test src/review/core.test.ts`. Three mutations, one direction each:
| mutation | caught? | |---|---| | revert the expansion's location gate in `expandScopePathsForArchiveIdentity` | **yes** — 170 pass / 1 fail, the `design-context.xml` fire direction at `src/review/core.test.ts:1027` | | make `isReviewedChangeSpecOrPlanPath` read `planLocation` (the spec forbids it) | **yes** — 169 pass / 2 fail, at `:1008` and `:1449` | | **add the sibling exemption into `auditWriteEvidenceOutsideScope`** | **NO — 171 pass / 0 fail, exit 0** |
**The third is the one the design forbids.** `AC-WRITE-EVIDENCE-KEPT` states the discriminating breach and names its own failure condition — *"WriteEvidence helper skips those paths"* — and no test in the file detects that. The reason is precise: the sibling is keyed on `identity.changeId` and **fails closed**, so the existing fixture (`raise: undeclared non-lifecycle .ngrace/ path (approved-spec shape)`, WriteEvidence path `.ngrace/changes/active/C-X/spec.xml`) passes no matching identity. Under the mutation the sibling returns `false`, the path still raises, and the assertion still passes. The pin observes the *behaviour* and not the *mechanism*, so it cannot see the mechanism being subverted.
**Why this is not a nit.** The whole architecture of this bundle is "sibling, never a widening", because the two audits share `isCliLifecyclePath` and widening it would silence a real breach signal ([F155.1](#f155.1)). The suite therefore protects the two directions that were *discussed* and leaves unguarded the one that was *decided*. A future simplifier who folds the sibling into the WriteEvidence audit gets a green suite and a silent breach detector.
**The general rule, and it is the third recurrence of one idea.** [F157](#f157) recorded that four tests used an artifact path as the vehicle for a property belonging to the expansion, so they would pass vacuously once artifact paths went silent. This is the same shape one level up: **a stay-true pin must be verified against the mutation it forbids, not merely observed to pass.** "The existing test stays green" is not a criterion — green is the state before *and* after the defect. Every `Failure conditions:` clause a spec writes is a mutation somebody must actually perform.
**Not an amendment.** `AC-WRITE-EVIDENCE-KEPT` is an approved criterion whose stated failure condition goes undetected, so the criterion is **not yet satisfied** and the remedy is inside T-001's existing scope (`src/review/core.test.ts` is in `ObservedWriteScope`). The added test is a **pin, not a red** — the property is HEAD-true; it is the *fixture* that was blind — so manufacturing a red for it would violate [F45](#f45).
**Found by probing, not by reading.** The authority read the production diff and judged it correct, which it is. The gap was in what the tests could see, and only a mutation showed it. Reading a diff cannot verify a test's discriminating power; only breaking the code can.

Finding.Title: ### F162 — what this repository's own source carries of GRACE's source-code conventions, measured, and the conditional-validator hole beneath it. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-05** at `30dea04`, prompted by the maintainer asking why our own code does not follow the GRACE rules for comments and logging. The premise was **half right, and the half that is right is the deeper half.**
**Layer by layer, whole populations. Denominator: 65 non-test `.ts` files under `src/`** (`find src -name '*.ts' ! -name '*.test.ts' | wc -l`).
| convention | required at | carried | ruled? | |---|---|---|---| | `START_MODULE_CONTRACT` / `LINKS:` | `semantic-markup.md:7` | **65 / 65** | yes | | `START_CONTRACT:` per exported declaration | `semantic-markup.md:73-83` | **0 / 65** | **no** | | `START_BLOCK_` / `END_BLOCK_` | `semantic-markup.md:85-106` | **0 / 65** | **no** | | `[Module][fn][BLOCK_]` log markers | `semantic-markup.md:108-119` | **0 of 7 call sites** | **no** |
**The module layer is genuinely adopted.** All 65 carry `LINKS:`, corroborated by a second instrument — `ngrace lint --path .` reports `Files checked: 114 / Governed files: 65`, matching the non-test population. **Precision limit, stated rather than hidden:** that is equality of *counts*, not proof of equality of *sets*.
**The two layers below it are absent, and every apparent hit is the checker checking itself.** `START_CONTRACT:` appears in exactly one non-test file, `src/project-utils.ts:269,338,339,349,664` — the regex and the error-message text that *implement* detection of the marker. `START_BLOCK_` appears in six, all either implementation (`src/review/core.ts:729,734`; `src/lint/catalog.ts:117,121,126`) or synthetic sample-source fixtures. Against an approximation of **433** exported declarations in those 65 files (`grep -E '^export (async )?function|^export const|^export class'` — an approximation, stated as one: it misses default exports, re-exports and multi-line signatures), the count of real function contracts is **zero**.
**Logging.** `logger.` occurrences: **0**. `console.log|console.error|console.warn`: **7**, all in `src/gates/command.ts` and `src/review/command.ts`, none carrying the `[Module][fn][BLOCK_…]` shape. User-facing output does not go through a logger at all: `formatGateEvaluation` (`src/gates/command.ts:66`), `formatReviewResult` (`src/review/core.ts:2078`) and `formatTextReport` (`src/lint/core.ts:780`), plus **63** `process.stdout.write` / `process.stderr.write` sites. The methodology already anticipates this shape for library-like code — `references/languages/rust.md:60-62` permits proving behaviour by `TraceAssertion` where log markers are not natural — but **that permission has never been claimed for this repository**, which is the point below.
**Adjacent populations, for completeness.** `src/*.test.ts`: 49 files, 14 carry `LINKS:`, 35 do not, and `semantic-markup.md:41` only *recommends* the structure for tests — no ruling exists either way. `scripts/`: 23 files, 6 of 12 non-test carry `LINKS:` (all pointing at an `M-RELEASE-AUTOMATION` the graph does not declare) and 0 of 11 tests do.
**What is ruled, and what is not — searched, not assumed.** The only on-point ruling is `.ngrace/changes/archive/C-ABSENCE-VALUE/spec.xml:51`, *"Adding START_MODULE_CONTRACT markup to src/ files (Path-only graph ownership remains deliberate and thin)"*, joined by the `scripts/` deferral at `C-ABSENCE-VALUE/spec.xml:49`, `C-GATE-SURFACE/spec.xml:121`, and the measurement behind it at `docs/plans/archive/RM-AGENT-RELIABILITY-EVIDENCE/plan.md:751-756` (*"deliberately deferred, not overlooked"*, 20 errors, *"not a thin slice"*) and `RM-AGENT-RELIABILITY/plan.md:2037-2060`. **Nothing anywhere rules on function contracts, block markers, or the logging convention for this repository's own source.** Searches that returned nothing on point: `START_CONTRACT`, `START_BLOCK`, `logging convention` and `logger\.` across `decisions.md`; `NonGoal` across every archived `spec.xml` filtered for contract/block/logging. `C-CONTRACT-DEBT` and `C-EXECUTION-CONTRACT` are false positives — API error contracts and the execution protocol, not semantic markup. `C-FAILURE-LOCALIZATION/spec.xml:222` assumes `START_BLOCK_` anchors in **target** projects GRACE verifies, not here.
**The hole, and it is [F147](#f147)'s class.** No rule fires on a source file that simply lacks a contract. `markup.unknown-link` (`src/lint/catalog.ts:159-167`) validates a `LINKS:` that already exists; `graph.module-without-linked-files` (`:168-177`) fires **graph→file**, only where a module already declares a `Path`. Across roughly 95 rule ids there is no `markup.missing-module-contract` and no equivalent, and no test asserts one. **Consequence:** a new `src/` file added tomorrow with no markup does not error — it silently stops being counted among governed files, and the repository stays green while shrinking its own governed surface. The 65/65 is a hand-maintained convention, not a ratchet. This is the same shape [D28](#d28) was written to fix in `decisions.md`, one layer down and in the product rather than the record.
**A path in the ruling was wrong and is corrected here.** The maintainer's scope named `src/commands/**`; **that directory does not exist** (`ls -d src/commands` → No such file or directory). The command surface as it stands is `src/grace.ts`, eleven `src/grace-*.ts` modules, and `src/gates/command.ts`, `src/review/command.ts`, `src/query/command.ts`. The spec binds the real paths.
**Method note, recorded because it nearly produced a false number.** The authority's first verification pass passed an unquoted multi-line variable as a file list; zsh does not word-split, the grep binary took the whole list as one filename, and both counts came back `0` — a plausible answer that would have confirmed the claim under test for the wrong reason. Re-measured with `find … -print0 | xargs -0`. Read a zero from a search the same way as any other result: only after confirming the search ran.

Finding.Title: ### F161.1 — six corrections to [F161](#f161), five of them measurements F161 itself took, and one correction to the correction. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
The executor authoring `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT`'s spec re-measured every count in [F161](#f161) and returned six in its `WRONG` field. Each was verified independently by the authority before being recorded here. **Four were exact, one understated the defect, and one was itself wrong.**
1. **The literal-path count carried the filename's number.** F161 wrote *"45 archived artifacts cite the literal path"*. Measured under `.ngrace/changes/archive/`: the literal path `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md` appears in **22** artifacts (16 `spec.xml`, 6 `plan.xml`); the bare filename `decisions.md` appears in **45** (30 `spec.xml`, 15 `plan.xml`). The label of one measurement was written onto the count of the other. **CONFIRMED.**
2. **A two-level heading cut omits 63 entries.** F161's *"200 `### F<n>` / 20 `## D<n>`"* misses **27** `#### F` findings and **36** `### D` sub-decisions. Preservation cannot be defined on the two-level cut. **CONFIRMED.**
3. **The anchor counts moved and the anchors do not resolve.** 465 + 63 at F161's commit; **476 + 74** at `30dea04`; **568** total `(#f…)`/`(#d…)` occurrences at `b0adb69` under a wider pattern. More important than the drift: of 180 distinct anchor targets, **0 resolve under GitHub heading-slug rules** — the real slug of F161's own heading is `f161--what-decisionsmd-actually-is-measured-and-the-four-…`, not `f161`. **179 of 180 resolve only under a first-token convention**, and `f21-correction` resolves under neither. F161's *"528 internal links must be rewritten, not broken"* assumed a resolution that does not exist: they are already broken, and the split's `<a id>` anchors are what will make them work for the first time. **CONFIRMED, and the defect is larger than the correction said.**
4. **There is no execute-skill pin.** F161 said `scripts/skill-contracts.test.ts` pins the file in *"the status rules, an execute step, plan rule 15 and the reviewer skill"*. The four sites are `scripts/skill-contracts.test.ts:420` (`ngrace-spec` status_rules), `:432` (`ngrace-spec` workflow step 6), `:511` (`ngrace-plan` must-do rule 15), `:578` (`ngrace-reviewer`). `ngrace-execute/SKILL.md` is read at `:129,143,343,362` and none of those assertions names the file. **CONFIRMED.**
5. **Heading-token collisions: F161 recorded none, and the correction named the wrong three.** Under the first-token slug rule the spec proposed (`F108.1 → f1081`), `F9.1` and `F91` both reduce to `f91`. Measured at `b0adb69`: **259 distinct first-token ids, 28 colliding groups** — `F9.1`–`F9.9` against `F91`–`F99` (nine groups), `F10.1-3`×`F101-103`, `F11.1-2`×`F111-112`, `F12.1-2`×`F121-122`, `F13.1-2`×`F131-132`, `F5.1`×`F51`, `F8.1-2`×`F81-82`, `F27.1`×`F271`, `F21`×`F21 correction`, `D1.1`–`D1.4`×`D11`–`D14`, `D2.1`×`D21`. The executor's `WRONG` named the set as `{F21, F19, F27.1}`; **`f19` does not collide with anything** (`F19.1`→`f191`, `F19's…`→`f19s`). Right instinct, sampled population — the same error class as [F130.1](#f130.1) and [F157](#f157), found this time in the executor's report rather than the authority's.
6. **Not an error:** 9940 versus 10073 lines is the three commits after `9b27238`, not a bad measurement at F161's own commit.
**A seventh fact, measured here and named by neither side.** **73** anchor occurrences across **25** distinct ids cite a colliding token (`d11` ×8, `f95` ×7, `f93` ×7, `f82` ×6, …). These are broken today, so nothing regresses now — but once explicit ids exist, `(#f93)` resolves to whichever heading holds `f93`, and every one of those 73 that *meant* `F9.3` will land silently on `F93` instead. **A reference that resolves to the wrong entry is worse than one that resolves to nothing**, because nothing announces it. A delimiter-preserving slug rule fixes the *targets* and leaves these 73 *citations* to be resolved by reading each one.

Finding.Title: ### F163 — the authority mutated the record that an in-flight bundle had been dispatched to measure. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
`C-RECORD-RETIREMENT`'s brief was handed over at **14:0x** telling the executor to re-measure `decisions.md` itself; the spec was authored at **14:08** against `30dea04`; the authority committed `b0adb69` — [F162](#f162) and [D29](#d29), 134 lines into that same file — at **14:21**. Six of the spec's Constraints were false within thirteen minutes of being written: four line/byte counts, two heading counts, the four ceiling bases, and — the one that is not a stale number but an incomplete set — *"Live chartered names remaining (10)"*, enumerated by name, which `D29` made twelve.
**The general shape:** the authority's standing duty to record findings in `decisions.md` is in direct conflict with any bundle that takes `decisions.md` as its subject. Every finding recorded during such a bundle invalidates its spec. This is not specific to this bundle — it is the reason the record needs a form the authority can append to without moving the measurements a spec depends on.
Paid by [D30](#d30).

Finding.Title: ### F165 — `C-SCOPE-AUDIT-ATTRIBUTION-2` changed what a plan-approve review reports and left the skill teaching the old behaviour. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured 2026-09-05 at `ed6d1b8`, on the first plan-approve review run after that bundle merged.
`skills/ngrace/ngrace-plan/SKILL.md` rule 15 teaches: *"At plan-approve `review.scope-outside-write-scope` on the bundle's own `spec.xml`, `plan.xml`, and (when that file changed) `decisions.md` is **expected**; do not add those paths to `ObservedWriteScope`."* **Neither `spec.xml` nor `plan.xml` fires any more** — the identity-keyed sibling predicate silences them, which is precisely what that bundle shipped and what its close measured (67 errors → 0 on a re-review). The sentence now describes behaviour the product no longer has.
**And the path that does still fire is not named.** `design-context.xml` is the bundle's own authoring-pass artifact, is not gate-stamped, and is therefore outside the sibling predicate. On `C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR` it raises `review.scope-outside-write-scope` as an **error** at every `--change` review, with no remedy the rule offers: adding it to `ObservedWriteScope` is what rule 15 forbids, and would in any case assert that the plan writes a file it does not.
**The bundle that caused it touched no skill.** `git log -- skills/ngrace/ngrace-plan/SKILL.md` ends at `75754a7` (PR #68, `C-APPROVE-TIME-REVIEW`); the attribution bundle merged as PR #71 and modified no `SKILL.md`. A behaviour change shipped without its teaching.
**Size of the repair, measured rather than estimated.** The sentence is pinned at **four** assertion sites in `scripts/skill-contracts.test.ts` — `:417/:421` (spec `status_rules`), `:429/:433` (spec workflow step 6), `:508/:512` (plan must_do rule 15), and the reviewer block at `:570` — and lives in the canonical skill plus a **byte-identical** packaged mirror (`diff -q` reports no difference), so `validate-marketplace` holds them together. Executor-sized, not a one-line fix.
**Precedent for the disposition, checked before ruling.** Of 65 archived bundles, 7 carry a `design-context.xml`, and **3 of those list it inside `ObservedWriteScope`** — `C-APPROVAL-FINGERPRINT`, `C-CRITERION-CLOSE-EVIDENCE`, `C-SUPERSEDE-COMMAND`. That is the practice rule 15 forbids, appearing three times before rule 15 existed. **Precedent lost to the shipped rule**: the executor's refusal to widen the scope is correct, and the finding is acked at close rather than silenced.

Finding.Title: ### F166 — the readings were derivable after all: the link text names the target in 565 of 568 citations. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured 2026-09-05 at the close of `C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR`'s execution, as the authority's audit of `AC-AMBIGUOUS-READ`.
The spec's premise was that no rule derives an ambiguous citation's target — *"each `(#f93)` means either `F9.3` or `F93`, and only the citing sentence says which"*. **That is false for all but three of them.** Every in-scope citation carries its target's identifier in its own **link text**: `[F9.3](#f93)` names `F9.3`. Comparing the F/D token in the link text against the destination resolves **565 of 568** mechanically. The three exceptions are prose labels, not F/D tokens — `[P1.12](#f38)`, `[P1.13](#f39)`, and ``[`C-REPORT-HONESTY`](#f14)``.
**The audit that proved it also proved the work correct.** Run over the post-execution file, every one of the 568 destinations agrees with its own link text, which is a stronger result than reading 79 sentences would have given, and it covers all 568 rather than the 79 the plan scoped.
**Consequence, and it is a strengthening rather than a criticism.** The bundle's own declared blind spot — a citation repointed to a wrong-but-existing anchor, which `AC-AMBIGUOUS-READ` calls unmechanizable and which the authority confirmed by planting `[F9.3](#f93)` on a throwaway copy and watching `validate-citation-anchors.ts` exit **0** — **is mechanically catchable** by a text-versus-destination consistency check. The validator ships without one. Adding it would close the one class the bundle knowingly leaves open, and the three prose-label exceptions are a small allowlist, not an obstacle.
**Not grafted.** Scope landed before approval; this belongs to a later bundle, not to a plan whose task population is frozen and already executed.

Finding.Title: ### F167 — two citations name a sub-decision and point at its parent, and this bundle is what makes them fixable. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
`[D1.5](#d1)` at line 5651 (*"following D1.5's precedent"*) and `[D5.2](#d5)` at line 6389 (*"Under D5.2"*). Both are **pre-existing** — present unchanged at `bf0d530` before execution and after — and both are outside `C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR`'s population: `#d1` and `#d5` are not colliding strip-dot tokens, they resolve correctly as ids, and they fall in the 380-occurrence already-keep class.
They are wrong only in precision: the reader lands on the parent decision and must find the subsection. **Until this bundle ran, there was nothing better to point at** — `d1.5` and `d5.2` did not exist as anchors. Now they do.
Found by [F166](#f166)'s text-versus-destination audit, which is the check that would have caught them automatically had it existed. Two links, one bundle's worth of nothing — but recorded rather than silently fixed, because grafting a repair onto an executed plan's frozen population is how a task list stops describing the work.

Finding.Title: ### F168 — the second supersede of the week, and what it is and is not worth to the pilot question. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured 2026-09-05 after `C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR` was superseded by `C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR-2`.
**The counter.** `supersede-depth=1` on **both** current replacements — `C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR-2` and `C-SCOPE-AUDIT-ATTRIBUTION-2` — confirming that the depth increments on the replacement and not on the abandoned bundle. **Ten** bundles on disk carry `status="superseded"` on the spec **root element** (`C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR`, `C-CURSOR-TASK-IDENTITY`, `C-CURSOR-TASK-SENTINEL`, `C-LEDGER-READ-ABSENCE`, `C-LINT-PHASE-HONESTY`, `C-PHASE-RULE-PIN`, `C-SCOPE-AUDIT-ATTRIBUTION`, `C-SUPERSEDE-RECORD`, `C-SUPERSEDE-VERB`, `C-VERDICT-EVIDENCE`) — matched on the root element rather than on the token anywhere in the file, because `status="superseded"` also appears inside Constraint prose.
**[D23](#d23) decides pilot on `supersedeChainDepth`, so this entry records what this instance is worth to that decision — and it is worth less than it first looks.**
**The case for it as pilot evidence.** The defect reached an approved plan through the full ceremony: authority brief, executor authoring, authority verification including an `AcceptanceCriteria` read and an `F136` anchor check, a clean approve-time review, and maintainer ratification on the closed lexicon. It became visible only when the executor ran T-006 and the command exited 1. That is the shape pilot exists to catch.
**The case against, and it is the honest half.** It was **catchable by reading**. The plan listed `lint --path . --fail-on warnings` as a task verification; the execute skill's own assertion-mode table (`skills/ngrace/ngrace-execute/SKILL.md:11`) defines `--assertions current` as the preflight **before** observed writes. Checking each Verification command against that table would have caught it at plan review. The authority did not perform that check. So this is a **review miss**, not a demonstration that review is incapable — and the previous supersede was confounded the other way, by an authority error rather than a review miss.
**What it therefore adds to the pilot file:** one unconfounded instance of the ceremony passing a defect that execution then exposed, weakened by the fact that a check the authority already owed would have found it. A pilot execution would have caught it; so would a checklist. **The cheaper remedy is named here so the pilot discussion has to answer it:** verify every task Verification command's assertion mode against the skill table at plan review, before approving.

Finding.Title: ### F169 — the `--assertions current` rule needs no teaching change; it needs the detector it already has, pointed at the element it does not inspect. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured 2026-09-05 at `5f20c72`, answering whether the skills need adjusting after [F168](#f168)'s supersede.
**The teaching is already correct, explicit, and in the right skill.** `skills/ngrace/ngrace-plan/SKILL.md:105`: *"Never put `--assertions current` in task verification that runs after writes. Use selected target/final lint externally instead."* And `:104` forbids a current-mode lint of this project root in `MustPassCommand`. **No skill edit is warranted** — the superseded plan violated a rule that was already written down in imperative form, and the authority approved it without checking against that line.
**The detector exists and is better than the registry says.** `isCurrentModeLintOfThisProjectRoot` (`src/artifact/assertions.ts:279-305`) recognises the lint subcommand in both `ngrace lint` and `src/grace.ts lint` forms, and `isCurrentAssertionMode` (`:262-266`) returns true when **no** `--assertions` token is present at all — `hasCurrent || !hasAssertionsToken`. **The "implicit-`current` gap" that `C-PHASE-RULE-PIN`'s registry row describes is therefore already closed**; that row's claim, written 2026-08-31, is stale and must be re-derived before that bundle is briefed ([F123](#f123)).
**The live gap is section coverage, not mode detection.** `assertions.ts:299` returns early unless `section === "TargetAssertions"` **and** `assertion.kind === "MustPassCommand"`. A task's `Verification` commands are never passed to the check. The superseded plan's T-006 carried `bun ./src/grace.ts lint --path . --fail-on warnings` — no `--assertions` token, so implicitly current-mode, on this project root — inside a task `Verification`, and lint reported **0 errors, 0 warnings** on that plan at both approve-time reviews.
**Disposition.** This belongs to `C-PHASE-RULE-PIN` (registry row 7), whose charter is exactly *"reconcile the plan skill's `MustPassCommand` restriction with the contract the linter actually enforces"*. Its charter needs two corrections before briefing: the implicit-mode half is already shipped, and the unenforced half is the section restriction at `:299`. Widening that check to task `Verification` commands would have refused the superseded plan at authoring time, before an approval, an execution and a supersede were spent on it.
**Correction to [F168](#f168).** That finding offered "a checklist" as the cheaper remedy to a pilot execution. The cheaper remedy is not a checklist — it is a five-line widening of a detector this repository already ships, and the pilot discussion should weigh it as such.

Finding.Title: ### F170 — the replacement bundle's evidence contract carried four close-evidence commands that cannot fail, three of them inherited from the bundle it replaces. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured 2026-09-06 at `5f20c72`, on the authority's verification of the `C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR-2` spec before approval.
`gate verdict` executes `CloseEvidence` commands (`src/gates/ledger.ts:406`) and refuses to record `outcome="pass"` on a non-zero exit. A command that always exits 0 therefore records a pass that carries no information. **Four of the spec's seven criteria had one.**
**The mechanism.** A bare `git diff --exit-code -- <paths>` compares the working tree against `HEAD`. The close ceremony commits. By the time `gate verdict` runs, the tree is clean and the command exits 0 whatever was written. Probed on a throwaway clone: a committed edit to `decisions.md` and `scripts/validate-citation-anchors.ts` leaves `git diff --exit-code -- <the four production paths>` at **0**, while `git diff --exit-code 5f20c72 -- <the same paths>` exits **1**.
- **`AC-NO-PRODUCTION-WRITE`** — prose demanded a diff *"against the tree at plan approval"*; the command diffed against `HEAD`. The sentence and the command made different claims. - **`AC-DOCS-EXAMPLES`** — same bare form over `README.md examples/`. - **`AC-NO-ARCHIVE-WRITE`** — bare, **and** its prose was falsified by its own close: it forbade any changed path under `.ngrace/changes/archive/`, which is exactly where `gate archive` moves the bundle. Probed: base-pinned over the whole archive exits 1 at close; with a pathspec exclusion of the bundle's own directory it exits 0, and still exits 1 on a planted edit to the predecessor's ledger. The command as written checked only `docs/plans/archive/`, so it under-claimed the prose. - **`AC-VALIDATOR-CI`** — asserted *"package.json validate:ci invokes validate:citation-anchors"* with `bun test scripts/validate-citation-anchors.test.ts` as its only evidence. That test never reads `package.json`. Probed on a clean clone with `&& bun run validate:citation-anchors` deleted from `validate:ci`: **13 pass, 0 fail**.
**`change.close-evidence-undiscriminating` does not catch this class, and says so.** `C-EVIDENCE-DISCRIMINATION` shipped the rule with the limit written into its own explanation — *"git diff --exit-code over the wrong paths still exit 0. A green rule is not evidence that the harder check happened."* Lint reporting 0/0 on the spec is not a defence, and the authority nearly treated it as one. **The linter's silence is the cheap class passing, not the criterion discriminating.**
**Inheritance, measured over the population.** Of 13 `git diff` close-evidence commands across the 66 archived bundles, **11 pin an explicit base commit** and **2 are bare** — and both bare ones are in `C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR`, the superseded bundle this one replaces. The replacement carried its predecessor's weakest convention forward while fixing the defect it was cut to fix. **A supersede re-ratifies the parts nobody re-examined.**
**Two counts of the authority's own that were wrong before the probe corrected them**, both the [F164](#f164) class of a pattern silently defining its population: `\[TEXT\]\(#[fd][^)]*\)` returned 569 fragments and 4 non-F/D link texts because `#decision-candidate--…` begins with a `d`; constrained to `#[fd]\d`, the executor's **568** and **3** are exact. And `dest == lower(token)` reported 3 destination mismatches by ignoring the qualifier-suffix rule that makes `[F21 correction](#f21-correction)` correct; the executor's **563 / 2** holds. **Every number in the spec's `Assumptions` block survived re-measure; both corrections were the authority's.**
**Also not a defect, recorded because the absence nearly became a claim.** No archived plan has an empty `ObservedWriteScope` — all 64 carry at least one `File`/`Glob`, minimum 1 at `C-REASON-CONSTANTS` — which invited the conclusion that this bundle's `<None />` scope was unbuildable. It is the documented idiom (`skills/ngrace/ngrace-plan/SKILL.md:60,62`; `OBSERVED_SCOPE_DIRECT_TAGS` at `src/artifact/grammar.ts:245`; the plan template itself). The absent precedent meant only that no prior bundle had zero writes. **The population count answered a different question than the one being asked** — [CLAUDE.md](../../../../CLAUDE.md)'s rule 2, caught before it reached a brief.
Nine of the 64 archived plans do not parse as strict XML (unescaped `<` or `&` in prose, the [F43](#f43) class); the counts above cover all 64 by parsing 55 and text-scanning the remaining 9.

Finding.Title: ### F171 — the detector meant to prevent this bundle's originating defect does not recognise the house command form, and [F169](#f169) named the wrong gap. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured 2026-09-06 at `d6a64a6`, while verifying `C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR-2`'s plan.
`C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR` was superseded because its T-006 task `Verification` carried `bun ./src/grace.ts lint --path . --fail-on warnings` — a current-mode lint of this project root, after writes. [F169](#f169) examined the guard and ruled that *"the teaching is already correct"*, that `isCurrentModeLintOfThisProjectRoot` *"recognises the lint subcommand in both `ngrace lint` and `src/grace.ts lint` forms"*, and that the single live gap is the section restriction at `src/artifact/assertions.ts:299`, which never passes task `Verification` commands to the check. It concluded that widening that check *"would have refused the superseded plan at authoring time"*.
**It would not have.** `invokesNgraceLintSubcommand` (`src/artifact/assertions.ts:257-260`) is two alternations, each allowing an optional `bun run ` prefix and an optional `./`. Neither admits a bare `bun ` before a `./`-prefixed path. Probed over six variants of the same command:
| form | detected | |---|---| | `bun ./src/grace.ts lint --path . --fail-on warnings` | **no** | | `bun run ./src/grace.ts lint …` | yes | | `./src/grace.ts lint …` | yes | | `src/grace.ts lint …` | yes | | `ngrace lint …` | yes | | `bun run ngrace lint …` | yes |
**The one form it misses is the house form.** It is what the superseded plan wrote, and it is what this repository's own operating instructions mandate, because `bun run ngrace <args>` re-quotes arguments. The guard is blind precisely where the repository is required to aim it.
**Confirmed at three levels, because the regex reading alone is not evidence.** With `bun ./src/grace.ts lint --path . --fail-on warnings` planted inside `TargetAssertions/MustPassCommand` — the position [F169](#f169) says *is* covered — `lint --fail-on warnings` exits **0** with 0 errors and 0 warnings; `gate approve --artifact plan` returns **permit**; and the exported `extractAssertionsWithIssues(plan, "TargetAssertions")` returns the command as an extracted value with **zero issues**. The section restriction at `:299` was never reached, because the predicate returned false first.
**Consequence for the charter.** `C-PHASE-RULE-PIN` (registry row 7) now carries **two** corrections, not one. [F169](#f169)'s remedy — widening section coverage — is necessary and **not sufficient**: applied alone it would still have passed the superseded plan. The fix is two-part, command-form recognition **and** section coverage, and only the pair discriminates. A single-part fix would ship a guard that reports green on the exact defect that produced two supersedes.
**Not grafted.** This bundle's approved spec forbids editing `src/`, and its `ObservedWriteScope` is `<None />`; a production fix here would breach `AC-NO-PRODUCTION-WRITE`. The conflict is real and documented, which is the exception [D11](#d11) allows.
**The authority's own error, recorded against the brief that carried it.** The plan brief told the executor that a `design-context.xml` *"raises `review.scope-outside-write-scope` as an error at every `--change` review"*. That is false for an empty `ObservedWriteScope`: `src/review/core.ts:1068` continues past every changed file when scope files and globs are both empty, and `:1541-1549` sets the audit to `not-run` outright. Probed — a `design-context.xml` added under this bundle's empty scope reviews **0 findings**. [F165](#f165) measured its claim on `C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR`, which had a non-empty write scope; the authority restated a context-bound measurement as a universal. The advice to omit the file was still right, for a different and smaller reason: it is optional, and 8 of the 66 archived bundles carry one. Caught by the executor's `WRONG` field.

Finding.Title: ### F173 — the genre set's resolution base is unspecified, and one reading couples the validator's unit tests to repository state. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-06** at `11e2d51`, same verification pass.
The draft spec names the genre set as repository-root-relative paths, requires a planted sibling to fail *"even when argv is omitted **or points only at `decisions.md`**"*, and separately promises that *"argv still accepts a fixture path so existing tests keep working"*. It never says whether the set is anchored at the repository root or resolved relative to the argv target's directory.
The existing suite decides the stakes: `scripts/validate-citation-anchors.test.ts:12-29` writes each fixture as `decisions.md` inside an `mkdtempSync` directory and spawns the script with `cwd: REPO_ROOT`. Under a root-anchored genre set every fixture run would also read the repository's real record files, so a unit test's verdict would depend on the state of `decisions.md`. Under a target-relative set the fixture directory has no siblings and the existing tests are unaffected.
Target-relative is the only reading that satisfies both requirements at once.

Finding.Title: ### F174 — a SHA-pinned `git diff --exit-code` closes [F170](#f170)'s hole but still cannot see an untracked write. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-06** at `11e2d51`, probed in both directions on the working tree.
The draft spec applies [F170](#f170) correctly: both archive-protection close-evidence commands pin the commit rather than comparing against `HEAD`. Probed: perturbing one archived `spec.xml` exits **1**; restoring it exits **0**; the clean tree exits **0**. That half discriminates.
The residue is `git diff`'s own blind spot. A **new untracked** path under `.ngrace/changes/archive/` leaves the same command at **0**, while the criterion's failure clause claims *"a write to another archived bundle"* fails. Tracked edits and deletions are caught; a first-time write into an archived bundle is not. Either the prose narrows to staged or committed edits of tracked paths, or the evidence gains untracked coverage.

Finding.Title: ### F175 — one citation in the record has an empty destination, and it is outside every shipped check. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-06** at `11e2d51`. `decisions.md:9223` carries `[decisions.md:7525](#)` — a link whose destination is the empty fragment.
It is the single difference between the two population counts of the file: `\]\(#[^)]*\)` finds **644** and `\]\(#([^)]+)\)` finds **643**. `FRAG_RE` requires `[fd][0-9]`, so the citation validator never sees it, and it resolves to nothing in a browser.
Pre-existing; not introduced by `C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR-2` and not `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT`'s to fix under the freeze. Owner: whichever bundle next writes the record, or [F166](#f166)'s text-versus- destination check, which is the class that would catch it.

Finding.Title: ### F176 — the "a draft is corrected in place" half of the supersede rule is not in [D27](#d27); it is the residual of D27's scope. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-06** at `11e2d51`, raised by the executor's `WRONG` field against the authority's send-back brief and confirmed by reading the ruling.
[D27](#d27) (`decisions.md:10105-10110`) rules on **approved** artifacts only: *"When an approved spec or plan is found defective, the route is `ngrace supersede` and a replacement bundle."* It says nothing about drafts. The authority's brief wrote *"`D27` says it is corrected in place"*, and the standing session framing carries the same pairing.
**The practice is right and the citation is wrong.** A draft has no ratification to invalidate, so `supersede` has nothing to repair and in-place correction is what remains once `D27`'s scope is excluded. That is an inference from the ruling's boundary, not a sentence inside it, and it must be written that way: a true conclusion resting on a citation that does not carry it. Anyone checking `D27` for the draft half finds nothing and is entitled to conclude the practice is unfounded.
Cite it as *"outside `D27`'s scope"*, never as *"`D27` says"*. If the distinction is worth binding, it needs its own ruling.

Finding.Title: ### F177 — fifteen archived bundles already cite a roadmap `plan.md` path that does not exist, and nothing detects it. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-06** at `408f2ae`, while surveying the cost of converting roadmap markdown to XML.
`docs/plans/active/RM-AGENT-RELIABILITY/plan.md` is cited by **15** archived bundles — `C-ABSENCE-VALUE`, `C-ADOPTION-SURFACE`, `C-ATTEMPT-LOG`, `C-CALIBRATION`, `C-CALIBRATION-CONTEXT`, `C-CALIBRATION-PROVENANCE`, `C-FAILURE-LOCALIZATION`, `C-GATE-RECORD-ABSENCE`, `C-GATE-SURFACE`, `C-GRAPH-COVERAGE`, `C-OBSERVABLE-CHECKS`, `C-PLAN-QUALITY`, `C-REVIEW-SURFACE`, `C-RUN-LEDGER`, `C-SELECTION`. **The path does not exist.** The file is at `docs/plans/archive/RM-AGENT-RELIABILITY/plan.md`; the roadmap was archived and the citations were not, because archives are immutable and cannot be.
Whole population of roadmap citations in archived `spec.xml` / `plan.xml`: **22** to an `active/<RM>/plan.md`, of which 15 are these and 7 point at `RM-GOVERNED-PATH/plan.md`, which does exist; plus **1** to `RM-GOVERNED-PATH/review.md`.
**Nothing detects it.** `scripts/validate-citation-anchors.ts` resolves one target (`DEFAULT_TARGET`, `decisions.md`) and reads no archived artifact; no lint or review rule resolves an outbound path written inside an archived bundle. The breakage is silent and has been for the life of the archive.
**Why it matters beyond itself.** [F161](#f161) constraint 1 — *retire cannot mean delete*, because archived artifacts cite the path — is treated as the binding reason `decisions.md` must survive. That constraint has **already been violated** for roadmap paths, unnoticed, by an ordinary archival. So the argument that "the path must keep resolving" is not currently enforced anywhere: it is a convention that has failed once at scale. Any layout that leaves a stub behind needs a **check** that the stub still resolves, or it decays exactly this way.
Owner: not `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2`, whose scope is the record genres. Repairing 15 immutable citations is impossible by construction; the tractable half is a validator that resolves outbound roadmap paths in archived artifacts and reports the dangling ones, which is [F166](#f166)'s text-versus-destination family one level out.

Finding.Title: ### F178 — a bundle that writes no `src/` file has **neither** scope guard, because one is skipped and the other is `src/`-only. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-06** at `b97c0aa`, on the executor's `WRONG` against the authority's plan brief, then re-probed independently.
**Too-much is skipped.** `change.plan-scope-exceeds-spec` iterates `specAnchors.size === 0 ? [] : planDurable` (`src/artifact/grammar.ts:2028`). The comment above it is explicit: *"Legacy specs describe AffectedAreas in prose, so there is nothing to exceed."* The intent is backward compatibility with old prose specs.
**But a spec that legitimately writes no graph module also has prose `AffectedAreas`** — that is the correct authoring for such a bundle, and `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2` is exactly it. The guard cannot tell the two cases apart, so a deliberate no-module spec **silently forfeits** the check. Probed: planting `<DurableScope><GraphAnchors><M-LINT-CATALOG /></GraphAnchors></DurableScope>` into the approved bundle's plan gives lint **exit 0, 0 errors, 0 warnings**, no finding. Restored.
**Too-little cannot fire either.** `change.graph-anchors-miss-write-scope` only considers paths for which `isModuleOwnableWritePath` is true, and that function returns false for anything not under `src/` and for every test file (`src/lint/core.ts:724-732`). This bundle's `ObservedWriteScope` holds 18 files — `docs/plans/**`, `scripts/**`, `CLAUDE.md`, `package.json` — and **not one** is `src/` non-test.
**So for this whole class of bundle — record work, documentation, `scripts/` tooling — neither direction binds.** Scope discipline is manual. The authority's plan brief asserted the too-much warning as live protection; it is not, for this spec. That claim was false and the executor's probe disproved it.
Owner: a later bundle, **not** this one. `C-MODULE-CONTRACT-GATE` (position 6 under [D34](#d34)) is the plausible home; **re-derive its charter row before briefing it** rather than assuming the fit. The remedy is not obvious: distinguishing "prose because legacy" from "prose because no module is written" needs a positive marker in the spec, which is a grammar change.

Finding.Title: ### F179 — the close sequence emits `terminal` too early, and it has now happened twice. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-06** at `401db34`, on the maintainer's question of whether this was a product bug or a sequence defect. **It is the sequence.**
**The mapping is deliberate, not broken.** `KNOWN_KIND_STATE` (`src/grace-cursor.ts:330-338`) maps `command-run` to `in-progress` with its own comment — *"Durable MustPassCommand/Budget evaluation evidence (C-CALIBRATION-COMMAND-EVIDENCE)"* — and `terminal` to `complete`. That is correct where commands run **while** the task is open.
**The shipped skill asks for less than the authority's sequence did.** `scripts/skill-contracts.test.ts:146` pins `ngrace-execute`'s sentence: *"after a fold, final run-commands writes loose events and archive requires no-open-epoch, so terminal the declared task and fold before gate archive."* That constrains **fold after terminal** and **final `--run-commands` not after the fold**. It says nothing about terminal preceding the final assertions. The authority's `§9` sequence wrote `terminal` → `--assertions final --run-commands` → `fold`, adding a constraint the skill never asked for, so `--run-commands` appends `command-run` events after the closing event.
**Population, and the instrument's limit stated with it.** **No archived `run-ledger.xml` carries a usable `seq` attribute** — all 51 report `seq` absent or `0` — so event order is read from **document order**, and that limit is part of the measurement rather than a footnote. Of 51 archived ledgers the last event is `terminal` in **46**; `command-run` in **2** — `C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR-2` (two `command-run` after terminal) and `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2` (seven) — `opened` in **2** (`C-CURSOR-TASK-RESOLVER`, `C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY`), and `discarded` in **1** (`C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR`, which has no terminal at all).
**So this is a recurrence, not a first.** `C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR-2` closed the same way one day earlier under the same sequence, and nobody noticed, which is the strongest argument that the fix belongs in teaching rather than in operator discipline.
**A precedent exists for a different remedy.** [D20](#d20)'s body records the close of `C-CURSOR-TASK-RESOLVER` as *terminal, fold, `--assertions final --run-commands`, terminal, fold*, review, verdicts — re-emitting terminal and re-folding after the assertions. It is the **only** archived bundle with two `terminal` events (1 of 64 checked). That remedy also ends with terminal last.
**Two candidate sequences, both ending terminal-last:**
1. **Swap** — `--assertions final --run-commands` → `terminal` → `fold`. Simplest; one closing event. Searched for a blocker: final mode gates on `status === "approved"` (`src/lint/core.ts:520`), which still holds at that point because the hand-write to `applied` comes later. No terminal or complete precondition on final mode was found. 2. **Re-terminal** — the `D20` precedent, `terminal` → `fold` → assertions → `terminal` → `fold`. Has run in production once; costs a second fold.
**Nothing blocked, which is why it survived two closes.** `gate archive` requires `no-open-epoch`, satisfied by an empty `run/` after the fold; it never reads the derived state. The casualty is display: an **applied, archived** bundle reports `State: in-progress` permanently, which reads as corruption to anyone running `cursor show`. Archives are never edited, so both stand as dated records.
**Authority instrument failure, recorded against this finding.** The first version of this entry claimed "50 of 51 have terminal as the last event, 0 have any event after terminal". That was produced by sorting on a `seq` attribute **that does not exist**, so every comparison was `0 > 0` and the "after" set was empty for all 51 — vacuously true, and it hid the `C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR-2` precedent. The same shape as the hygiene grep that returned 0 because zsh passed 18 paths as one filename. **When a whole-population check returns a suspiciously clean answer, verify the attribute the check depends on exists before reporting the number.**
Owner: the authority's `§9` sequence and handoff, corrected immediately; the teaching clause goes to `C-APPROVAL-SCOPE` under [D33](#d33).

Finding.Title: ### F182 — a 7 × median headroom persists a fractional line ceiling whenever the live count is even. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-06** at `26ce576`.
`validate-record-retirement.ts:565-566` sizes headroom as a multiple of `median()`, and `median()` returns the mean of the two middle values on an even population — a `.5` whenever those two differ by an odd number. The multiplier decides whether that half survives: `2 ×` always clears it, `7 ×` never does. So `headroom` and `ceiling` are written as non-integers, and the record carries a line budget like `ceiling="1886.5"`.
**Reachable in the next rewrite, not hypothetically.** After `C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY` retires the 44-line `D24`, the live H2 set is 23 entries with a median of 37 and an integer headroom of 259. **One** added decision of 38 lines or more makes it 24 entries with a median of 37.5, and the next `--retire` would persist `headroom="262.5"` / `ceiling="1886.5"`. If `D24` does **not** leave — `AC-FIRST-CODIFY` tags it only if the `C-REWORK-CIRCUIT` tests still pass — the very first rewrite persists 262.5 against base 1668.
**Not a correctness defect.** The read path is `Number(attrs.ceiling)` (`validate-record-retirement.ts:795`), not `parseInt`, so the comparison `liveSize > ceiling` is exact and nothing truncates. The cost is that a public methodology repository states a size budget in half lines, and the `ceiling-exceeded` message reads *"exceeds persisted ceiling 1886.5"*.
**Latent in shipped code, widened by this bundle.** The findings genre has shipped `7 ×` since the split; it has not fired only because its median is currently the integer 36. Moving rulings from `2 ×` to `7 ×` puts a second, smaller, parity-flipping population on the same path.
Owner: a later bundle. Not grafted into `C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY`, whose spec is approved and fingerprinted. The remedy is a rounding rule at the point of derivation, and the open question is which direction — rounding **down** is the only direction that cannot loosen a budget.

Finding.Title: ### F184 — the approved plan's `T-001` verification command exits 1 as written. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-06**, raised by the executor and confirmed.
`T-001`'s `Verification` is `lint --change C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY --assertions baseline` with no `--run-commands`. That query exits **1** with six `assertion.command-not-evaluated`. The baseline was taken with `--run-commands` (exit 0) and the target ran clean after `T-005`, so nothing was actually unverified — but the command as recorded in an approved artifact does not pass when run as written.
Harmless at close, which uses `--assertions final --run-commands`. It matters for anyone re-running a task's verification from the plan. The plan is approved and fingerprinted, so this is not repairable in place.
**Refined 2026-09-06 on `C-RETIREMENT-WINDOW`, where the obvious remedy proved too strong.** The authority briefed the rule as *"a recorded `Verification` command must be one that exits 0 as written"*. That is wrong as stated. Probed after approving that bundle's plan: `lint --change <C> --assertions target --run-commands` still exits **1**, and not for the predicted reason — the message is *"Cannot record command-run: no declared task is in scope"*, not `change-not-approved`. `--run-commands` records a `command-run` event, which needs an open cursor on a declared task, so the command is **unrunnable outside execution** by design and resolves at execution time rather than at approval. The executor predicted approval; both of us were wrong about the stage, in opposite directions.
The rule that survives: a recorded `Verification` command must exit 0 **at the stage it is meant to run**, and a plan should not be judged by running its execution-stage commands at plan time. `F184`'s original case is still a real defect, because `--assertions baseline` without `--run-commands` never resolves at any stage.

Finding.Title: ### F185 — a real-repository measurement test has no explicit timeout, so archiving the 70th bundle turned the suite red after the move. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-06**, during the close of `C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY`, post-archive.
`src/grace-context.test.ts:522` calls `buildTaskSlice` against the live package root for three named archive subjects. It carries **no explicit timeout**, so it inherits Bun's 5000 ms default. The `git mv` that archived this bundle took the archive from 69 to 70 directories, and the test now runs **~5240 ms**. Deterministic, not flaky: three consecutive isolated runs failed at 5236.80 / 5243.60 / 5245.86 ms.
**It is purely a timeout; nothing is logically wrong.** Probed in the discriminating direction: `bun test --timeout 20000` gives **1735 pass / 3 skip / 0 fail**, exit 0, with every assertion in that test holding. The product is correct and the suite is red only against the default clock.
**This is exactly [F100](#f100)'s class, and the two-verdict close is what caught it.** The executor's `bun test` was green and honest — it ran **before** the archive move. The failure exists only after it. A single-verdict close would have archived this bundle with a red suite and never displayed the criteria whose `CloseEvidence` is `bun test`.
**The defect is structural, not incidental.** A test whose purpose is to measure the *real* repository has a cost that necessarily grows with the repository, so a fixed default clock is the wrong constraint for it — and any bundle archived from here would have tripped it, independent of this one. The remedy is an explicit, generous timeout on that `it(...)`, not a fixture rewrite, which would destroy the measurement the test exists to take.
**It did not block the close, and the authority's first reading that it did was wrong.** Bare `bun test` is **not** a `CloseEvidence` command for this bundle; the criteria run `bun test <file>` against three named `scripts/*.test.ts` files, none of which is `grace-context.test.ts`. All fifteen `CloseEvidence` commands were re-run after the `git mv` and exit 0.
**The fix had to land after the close, not inside it.** `AC-NO-GRAMMAR`'s evidence is `git diff --exit-code <base> -- src/`, so any `src/` write inside the bundle fails it — the one-line timeout edit was applied, tripped that criterion, was reverted for the verdict, and re-applied as its own commit once the bundle was archived. The criterion's prose targets the grammar layer (`src/artifact/xml.ts`, `xml-serialize.ts`) but its command is repository-wide over `src/`; anyone writing a bundle that may need an incidental `src/` fix during close should scope that command to the files the prose actually names.

Finding.Title: ### F188 — a close-evidence pathspec that covers `.ngrace/changes/` without excluding its own bundle cannot pass. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-06** at the close of `C-RETIREMENT-WINDOW`.
`AC-RECORD-FROZEN` pins `git diff --exit-code <base> -- docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/ .ngrace/changes/`. Every bundle writes its own directory under `.ngrace/changes/`, and its spec and plan are committed after the base commit, so that diff is **never** empty at close. The criterion is unsatisfiable by construction, not by anything the bundle did.
**Measured, not inferred:** the diff contained exactly four files — the bundle's own `spec.xml`, `plan.xml`, `run.xml` and `run-ledger.xml` — and **zero** files outside its directory. The record subtree the criterion exists to protect is byte-identical to the base commit, so the criterion's **intent** was satisfied while its **command** could not be.
Its sibling `AC-NO-ARCHIVE-WRITE` carries exactly the term that would have fixed it: `':(exclude).ngrace/changes/archive/C-RETIREMENT-WINDOW'`. The two criteria were written together and only one got the exclusion.
**Consequence at close.** `gate verdict --outcome pass` refuses while any `CloseEvidence` command exits non-zero, so the second verdict was recorded as `unable-to-determine` with reason `close-evidence-command-unsatisfiable`. Nine of the ten close-bound criteria passed post-archive.
**The authority missed it at approval.** Two of the five pinned commands were probed in both directions before approving; this one was not, and no probe was run in the state that matters — after the bundle's own artifacts exist under a pinned path. **A close-evidence pathspec must be probed in the post-close state, not the pre-close one**, which is the same lesson as [F100](#f100) applied to pathspecs rather than suites.
Owner: a later bundle, as a rule that a `CloseEvidence` pathspec covering a bundle-bearing directory must exclude the bundle's own path.

Finding.Title: ### F191 — staged charter rows have no anchor, so every wrap projection folded them into the preceding decision. **[verified]**
Finding.Body: Measured **2026-09-07** on the staged buffer, after the authority staged a fifth charter row and the decisions wrap jumped 299 → 338 for an entry that added no decision. `parseFrozenMarkdown` identifies an entry by an `` anchor followed by a heading matching `[FD]\d`. A staged charter row (`## STAGED CHARTER ROW — …`) has **neither**, so it is not an entry, and the preceding entry's `bodyRaw` runs straight through it to the next anchor. Per staged decision, parser-boundary body versus its own prose: | | D27.1 | D32 | D33 | D34 | D35 | D36 | total | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | parser | 54 | 29 | 38 | 40 | **81** | **96** | 338 | | own prose | 53 | 28 | 37 | 39 | **24** | **29** | 210 | The entire 128-line discrepancy sits in `D35` and `D36`, the two decisions that happen to be followed by charter rows. The other four differ by one line, a trailing blank. **A correct flush does not produce the parser figure.** Charter rows become `` elements in `registry.xml`; their text never enters a `` body. So the honest projection of the decisions genre is **210**, and `1624 + 210 = 1834` against a ceiling of **1883** — it **fits, with 49 to spare**. Findings likewise: 607 against a window of 816. **The flush is not blocked, and was not blocked when three consecutive reports said it was.** The authority wrote "short by 40" repeatedly and the executor's report carried the same 299; both used the parser boundary without asking what it attributes charter-row lines to. This is the "right string, wrong position" class the record already names — a number measured by a rule nobody checked against the thing it was meant to project. **The parser figure is not meaningless — it is the cost of a naive automated flush**, one that takes `parseFrozenMarkdown`'s output directly. That such a flush would silently bury two charter rows inside two decision bodies is itself a defect in any future flush tooling, and the reason the two numbers must never be conflated again.

Finding.Title: ### F189 — retiring findings lowers the median, so the window gains less than the lines removed. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-07** on the `C-PAYMENT-RECORD` working tree, after the production `--retire`.
The window after a move is **not** `previous window + Δ_retired`. `H` is re-derived as `7 ×` the median of the **remaining** live findings, and retiring the largest entries pulls that median down. Measured: 8 elements totalling **571** lines left, the median fell **36 → 35**, so `H` fell **252 → 245** and the ceiling fell `min(7978, 7726 + 245)` = **7971**. The window came out at `7971 − 7155` = **816**, not the 823 that `252 + 571` predicts.
**The rule, stated so it can be planned against:** `window_gain = Δ_retired − (H_old − H_new)`. Here `571 − 7 = 564`, and `252 + 564 = 816`. The loss is small when the retired set is close to the median and grows as the set skews large — which is exactly how fuel gets chosen, since the audit that picks it ranks candidates by line count.
**Consequence for planning.** Any bundle sizing retirement fuel against a target must add a margin for the median shift, and must not quote `252 + Δ` as the resulting window. Both the authority's brief and the approved spec's `WINDOW ARITHMETIC` carried the naive form; the executor measured the real one and did not reconcile toward the brief.
Related but distinct from [F182](#f182), which is about the same `7 × median` producing a fractional value on an even population. This one is about the median **moving**.

Finding.Title: ### F190 — `--retire`'s span removal leaves its neighbours' indent behind, and the drift compounds on every move. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-07** on the `C-PAYMENT-RECORD` working tree, before and after the production move.
`removeSpans` deletes an element's span without consuming the leading indent of the line that follows, so every live element that sat after a removed sibling gains two spaces. Measured on `findings.xml` live `<Finding>` open tags — indent width to occurrence count:
| | 2 | 4 | 6 | 14 | |---|---|---|---|---| | at `82775a06` | 192 | 3 | 3 | 1 | | after this move | 177 | 9 | 4 | 1 |
The 4-space population tripled and the 6-space grew. The same pass left the retired sibling's appends at column 0, matching the previous `--retire`. The record already carried some drift before this bundle, which is how it went unnoticed.
**It compounds.** Each move shifts another cohort of survivors one level deeper, and nothing ever normalises them back. Over enough retirements the live genre files become progressively less legible in a repository whose product is methodology artifacts other people are meant to read.
**Not a correctness defect.** The XML stays well-formed, every validator exits 0, and entity counts are conserved across the move. It also does **not** show up in a byte-identity check of the file the move did not touch: `registry.xml`'s close tag drifted the same way and was restored by hand, which is why the live registry file is byte-identical to `HEAD` while `findings.xml` is not.
**Deliberately not fixed by `C-PAYMENT-RECORD`.** `removeSpans` is the shipped writer, not that bundle's product change, and touching it would have put the bundle outside its approved Constraints. Owner: a later bundle, as a normalising pass in the writer rather than a hand edit at close — a hand edit is what happened to the registry close tag here, and it does not scale.

Finding.Title: ### F193 — a genre that does not move has its window clamped back to `H`, so retirement's `Δ` survives only until the next `--retire`. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-07** on the `C-CODIFY-DECISIONS` working tree, before and after a decisions-only production move.
`--retire` rewrites **all seven** genre roots on any successful move, not only the genre that moved. For a genre where nothing moved, `ceilingBase` equals `base`, so the persisted ceiling becomes `min(previousCeiling, base + H)` and the window becomes **`min(previous_window, H)`** — monotonically non-increasing toward `H`.
Measured on `findings.xml`, where **no Finding moved**:
| | base | headroom | ceiling | window | |---|---|---|---|---| | before | 7601 | 370 | 7971 | **370** | | after a decisions-only `--retire` | 7601 | 245 | 7846 | **245** |
The 370 was the window that the preceding flush's retirement had opened. A move in an unrelated genre erased it and left `H = 7 × median = 245`.
**This weakens `C-RETIREMENT-WINDOW` considerably.** That bundle's premise is that retirement creates room for a flush. It does — but the room survives only until the next successful `--retire` in **any** genre. Retire findings to make space, retire a decision before flushing, and the space is gone. To use a window you must flush immediately after the move that opened it, with no intervening retirement anywhere, and nothing in the product or the record says so.
**Not the same as [F189](#f189)**, which is about `H` itself shrinking as the median moves. This is about the accumulated `Δ` above `H` being discarded whenever a different genre moves.
Owner: a later bundle. The candidate remedies — persisting the opened window rather than re-deriving it, or re-deriving only the genre that moved — are a design question, not a patch.

Finding.Title: ### F196 — `CloseEvidence` is evaluated only in the applied-archive state, and the skill that teaches criterion authoring never says so. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-08** at `54e26d9`, during review of `C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION`'s draft spec.
`isAppliedArchiveBundle` (`src/gates/ledger.ts`) requires **both** that the bundle path contain `/changes/archive/` **and** that the spec's `status` be `applied`; `evaluateCloseEvidenceChildren` returns an empty list otherwise. So every `CloseEvidence` command is measured in the **post-archive** state and in no other. A criterion whose truth depends on the pre-archive state is never evaluated in the state it describes.
**The instance.** That draft's `AC-CHARTER` asserted a live `registry.xml` row named for the bundle, absent from `registry-retired.xml`, whose name was absent from `.ngrace/changes/archive/`. All three clauses are **false** in the only state where the criterion is ever evaluated: the close creates that archive directory, which raises `registry-eligible-still-live`, and the retirement move puts the row in the retired sibling. `AC-FLUSH` had the same shape. The author was not careless — nothing told it which state its criterion would be measured in.
**Searched, not assumed.** `grep -rn 'CloseEvidence' skills/ngrace/`: the coupling appears **once**, at `ngrace-reviewer/SKILL.md:51` — *"An applied-archive `CloseEvidence` `AC-*` must have a recorded evaluation on a Verdict"* — as a rule about verdicts, in the reviewer's skill. `ngrace-spec/SKILL.md`, which teaches how to write the criterion, carries only an example at `:98` and never states the evaluation state.
Owner: a later bundle, on the teaching surface. The remedy is one sentence in `ngrace-spec` telling an author that a close criterion is measured after the archive move, and to write it invariant under that move.

Finding.Title: ### F197 — a finding can be paid by a sentence: `derivePayerMap` mints payments from prose, not only from `Pays`. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-08** at `54e26d9`, `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:466-497`, raised by the executor's `WRONG` field against the authority's claim that a row without `Pays` leaves a finding with no path out.
Beyond the `Pays` field of a chartered row, two prose paths mint payments:
- `closedWithTokens(row.statusText)` over an archived chartered row's `StatusText`, gated on the row's name being an archive directory; - a pass over **every** archived `spec.xml` that pays every `F`-token appearing in any sentence matching `PAID_FINDING_RE`.
**The consequence.** Eligibility is what `D28` and `D28.1` make the enforcement, and it can be minted by wording. An ordinary sentence in an archived spec that happens to match the pattern marks the findings it names as paid, and they become eligible for retirement on the next `--retire`. Nothing declares the payment; a phrase does.
**Observed cost, not theorised.** `C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION`'s spec carries a guard clause asserting that its own prose contains no sentence matching that pattern — a spec defending itself against its own text being read as a payment. That is the tax this path imposes on every future spec.
Owner: a later bundle. The remedy is a design question — narrow the prose paths to an explicit declaration, or keep them and make the derivation report what it minted and from which sentence — and the authority has no position yet.

Finding.Title: ### F198 — `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2` archived without a registry row, so the finding it settled is still live and cannot be paid. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-08** at `54e26d9`, during the `C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION` spec review, from the executor's `WRONG` field against the authority's brief.
[F172](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/findings.xml) is **live** (`findings.xml:7155`) and describes the citation validator's qualifier-suffix slug grammar — a mechanism that **no longer exists**. `expectedSlugFor` and `duplicateCount` are absent from `src/` and `scripts/` (0 hits), and the citation validator's only duplicate rule is `duplicate-id` over **index ids**, not tokens across layers. A split-token fixture drives all three record validators to exit 0. The mechanism was removed by `67bc55c` — `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2`, PR #74.
**The bundle that settled it has no row.** `grep -c '<Row name="C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2"'` returns **0** in `registry.xml` and **0** in `registry-retired.xml`, while the first `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT` has one. `derivePayerMap` keys payments on chartered rows gated on `archive.has(row.name)`, so a bundle with no row pays nothing: `F172` cannot become eligible by any path, and the live genre carries a finding whose subject was deleted two bundles ago.
**This is [F187](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/findings.xml)'s class surviving the bundle chartered to end it.** `C-PAYMENT-RECORD` recorded the payments that already happened; this is at least one it did not record. The population it missed is unmeasured here and must not be guessed — measuring it is part of the remedy, not a premise of it.
**Why it did not ride in `C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION`**, stated so the deferral is not silent: paying `F172` means creating a row for an already-archived bundle, whose `name` equals an archive directory on sight, and deciding what else `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2` settled. That is a population audit and a placement question, neither of which that bundle's approved scope answers, and grafting them in would contradict its own NonGoals. Surfaced to the maintainer as a charter candidate rather than filed.
Owner: the next charter decision.
**Cost already paid.** The authority's first spec brief carried `F172`'s headline as present behaviour, and the spec it produced repeated the claim in a Constraint until the executor measured it. A finding is never evidence of present state.

Finding.Title: ### F199 — `check-teaching-surface` refuses with zero bytes of output, and takes `validate:ci` red with it. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-08** at `8345933`.
`bun run ./scripts/check-teaching-surface.ts check` exits **1** while writing **0 bytes** to stdout and 0 to stderr. It names neither the file that failed, nor the rule, nor the missing text. It is a member of `validate:ci`, so the whole gate goes red with no message at all.
**Isolated by bisection, not inferred.** With a generated spec scaffold present under `.ngrace/changes/active/`, exit 1; with that one directory moved aside, exit 0; moved back, exit 1 again. The rule is `checkDocsAndExamplesDecision`: every **active** spec must mention `README.md` and `examples/` somewhere in a `Goal`, `Constraint` or `NonGoal`, and a freshly generated scaffold does not. Diagnosing this required reading the script, because the product said nothing.
**The cost is paid by every author of a new bundle**, since the window between `spec new` and a finished spec is exactly when the check fires — the moment a scaffold exists. A refusal that cannot be read is a refusal that gets worked around by deletion.
Owner: a later bundle. The remedy is small — name the file, the rule, and the missing tokens on the refusal path — but it is a product change to a `validate:ci` member and belongs in a chartered bundle.

Finding.Title: ### F200 — the authority offered amend-and-re-ratify as its recommendation, which [D27](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/rulings.xml) forbids, because it never searched the record. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-08**, during `C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION`'s plan stage.
On finding the approved plan self-contradictory, the authority put two variants to the maintainer and recommended *"correct the one clause, re-run the gate, re-ratify"*. [D27](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/rulings.xml) rules exactly the opposite: an approved governance artifact is repaired by **`ngrace supersede`** and a replacement bundle, and **amend-and-re-ratify is not available** until pilot is decided — *"permitted is not authorised"*. The maintainer's reply, *"supercede. no cheating"*, was enforcing a live ruling the authority had not read.
**The standing rule this broke** is the one in `CLAUDE.md`: *before proposing to change a behaviour, find the decision that created it* — a proposal may overturn a ruling, but it must say so and answer the argument. This proposal did neither, because no search was run.
**Second instance in one session of the same failure mode.** Earlier the authority put `F172`'s headline into a brief as present behaviour without checking whether the mechanism still existed; it had been deleted two bundles before, and the executor's measurement disproved it. Both are the same mistake: **acting on the record's contents from memory, or on their absence without a search.**
**Cost, exactly.** One full-bundle supersede — `C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION` archived, two ratifications discarded, a replacement bundle to be specced, planned and ratified from scratch — and one increment to `supersedeChainDepth`, which [D23](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/rulings.xml) makes the metric pilot is decided on. The defect it repairs was one sentence.
Owner: no bundle. This is a working-practice entry: the approval read must be end to end and must hunt self-contradiction, and any proposal touching governance must cite the ruling it obeys or overturns.

Finding.Title: ### F201 — the approved `C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION-2` spec carries a payer census that does not reproduce, and it stands uncorrected by ruling. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-08** at `5f5f95d`, raised by the executor's `DEVIATIONS` and re-derived independently by the authority.
The spec's payer-ground Assumption states that `derivePayerMap` over the live and retired registry rows *"(45 scanned) mints 52 payments"*. Driving the shipped function directly: **31 rows → 51 payments** through its own `PAYER_KINDS` filter (`chartered`, `historical`), and **45 rows → 51** unfiltered. **52 is reachable by no derivation**, so the figure was wrong when written, not expired.
